common_factors.text: Checkout fails only above a monetary threshold and succeeds below it — the single discriminating signature shared by every ticket in the cluster.
Failures concentrate on POST /v2/transactions: hard HTTP 500s in customer monitoring and 30-second request timeouts in the browser console.
Onset is the afternoon of 2026-08-11: first report says "since about 2:15 this afternoon", a second says "started today", and a third independently dates the 500s to "Tuesday afternoon".
Small orders placed as controls succeed during the same window: a €40 test order, a 5-seat license purchase, "smaller consumer orders", and "cheaper items".
Failure occurs before any payment network is contacted — customer banks show no charge attempt at all, consistent with a pre-authorization screening step.

Only one deploy in the pre-onset window semantically matches the symptom axis: d6 to payment-service, "Enable enhanced fraud screening for high-value transactions", shipped roughly 40 minutes before the first ticket.
Still active on day four with no mitigation, per the customer follow-up.

variations.text: Surfaced failure mode differs by report: error page, hard 500, 30-second timeout, white screen, and an infinite spinner — possibly one fault seen at different layers, possibly more than one.
Currency differs across reports — USD, EUR and JPY thresholds all reported — and the JPY figure (¥150,000) sits roughly an order of magnitude away from the ~1,000-unit boundary seen in USD/EUR.
Order size varies from just over the boundary (about $1,000–$1,300) to five-figure B2B restock carts.
Two tickets describe the failure without naming an amount (white screen; "big landscaping quotes"), so their threshold fit is inferred from order size language rather than a stated figure.
Segment varies: consumer retail, travel bookings, B2B distribution, school seat licenses, and trade quotes.
Reported browsers vary — Chrome and Edge, Safari on iPhone and Firefox, Chrome and Safari.

ruled_out.text: d5 (web-storefront seasonal theme/CSS refresh) is a poor fit: it shipped roughly two days before first report with no tickets in between, and an asset/CSS change does not produce server-side 500s or 30-second server timeouts.
Client-side or browser-specific cause ruled out: failures reproduce across Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (including Safari on iPhone).
Genuine card declines ruled out: banks show no charge attempt at all, so the request never reaches the payment networks.

Not a recurrence of a known issue: archive search returned only benign, unrelated older checkout tickets — a customization how-to, an expired discount code, and a rate-limit question. No prior instance of this signature.
Analytics/reporting timeout tickets surfaced by the same search are excluded from this cluster: no payment path and no threshold behavior. They were not investigated and should be triaged separately.

hypotheses.text: The enhanced fraud screening enabled by d6 rejects or hangs on transactions above its high-value threshold, causing /v2/transactions to 500 or time out before authorization is attempted. Support: d6 shipped about 40 minutes before the first ticket, its description names the exact axis every ticket reports, and banks see no charge attempt.
hypotheses.not_examined: No code, logs, or fraud-screening configuration were read; the trace attached to t228 was not opened; no rollback or mitigation test was performed.

hypotheses.text: The threshold is applied per-currency without FX normalization — a single numeric limit near 1,000 units applied to USD, EUR and JPY alike, which is why a ¥150,000 order (roughly $1,000 in scale terms is far below 150,000) trips the same limit as a $1,000 order.
hypotheses.not_examined: No threshold configuration, FX conversion logic, or per-currency limit table was inspected; the inference rests entirely on amounts quoted in ticket text.

hypotheses.text: The mixed failure surfaces (hard 500 versus 30-second timeout versus endless spinner) are one upstream fault manifesting at different layers — a screening call that hangs, then either times out at the gateway or returns 500 depending on client and timeout settings.
hypotheses.not_examined: No gateway/service timeout settings, retry behavior, or request traces were reviewed; whether these are one fault or two was not confirmed.

hypotheses.text: Impact skews toward the highest-value orders, so revenue loss per failure far exceeds an average failed checkout, and at least one confirmed customer defection has already occurred.
hypotheses.not_examined: No revenue or transaction telemetry was queried; the $18k figure is customer self-reported and unverified, and accounts a02–a09, a11, a12 were never looked up.

packet.packet_markdown:
# Escalation: Checkout fails above a ~1,000-unit local-currency threshold — POST /v2/transactions 500s and 30s timeouts since payment-service deploy d6

**Cluster:** 13 tickets / 12 customers · first seen 2026-08-11T14:14:00Z (t223) · still active day four (t248)  
**Requested severity:** P1 (explicitly requested by a10 in t230)

## Impact

- **Northwind Retail (a01)** — enterprise, NA, ~**$240k** ACV. Filed the first report (t223); escalated on day four self-reporting ~**$18k** in abandoned carts (t248).
- **Cardinal Foods (a10)** — enterprise, NA, ~**$190k** ACV. Requested P1; five-figure quarterly restock carts blocked (t230).
- ~**$430k** combined ACV across the two accounts checked (steps 3–4). The other ten accounts (a02–a09, a11, a12) were **not** looked up, so total exposure is higher and currently unquantified.
- EUR (t224, t233) and JPY (t238) amounts imply non-NA regions, but their account regions are unconfirmed.
- Severity is amplified by the failure mode: the bug blocks the **largest** carts specifically, so loss per failure is far above average, and at least one defection to a competitor is confirmed (t235).

## Evidence

| Fact | Cites |
|---|---|
| Onset 2026-08-11 ~14:15 — error page on Place Order, $2,300 cart screenshot, nothing changed customer-side | t223 |
| Only two deploys pre-onset; **d6** (payment-service, "Enable enhanced fraud screening for high-value transactions") shipped 2026-08-11T13:36:00Z — ~40 min before the first ticket | d6, d5, t223 |
| Three failures the same afternoon at ~€1,250 / €1,900 / €4,100; a €40 test order succeeded | t224 |
| `POST /v2/transactions` returning **500s** since "Tuesday afternoon", only "above four figures"; trace attached (not read) | t228 |
| Browser console shows `/v2/transactions` **timing out after 30 seconds** above ¥150,000; smaller consumer orders fine | t238 |
| Banks show **no charge attempt at all** on failed $1,600 / $2,050 orders — fails before the card networks | t226 |
| Reproduced on Chrome + Edge; Safari/iPhone + Firefox; Chrome + Safari | t230, t233, t246 |
| Below-threshold controls succeed: 5-seat purchase works vs 40+ seats stuck; "cheaper items go through fine" vs $1,300 patio set spinning forever | t241, t246 |
| Amount-less reports fit the pattern: white screen after submit, "big landscaping quotes" | t235, t245 |
| No prior instance of this signature in the archive — only benign unrelated checkout tickets | t101, t107, t108, search_ticket_history#2 |

## Merged note (visible only across tickets)

No single ticket names a threshold. Read together, the reports bracket one: **every** failure is above ~1,000 units of local currency — $2,300 (t223); €1,250 / €1,900 / €4,100 (t224); $1,600 / $2,050 (t226); "above four figures" (t228); >€1,000 (t233); >$1,000 (t243); $1,300 (t246) — while **every** stated success is well below it: €40 (t224), 5 seats (t241), "cheaper items" (t246), "smaller consumer orders" (t238).

The sharper cross-ticket fact: the boundary looks like the same **bare number** in each currency, not the same **value**. ¥150,000 fails (t238), roughly an order of magnitude above the ~$1,000 / €1,000 boundary in USD/EUR terms (t233, t243, t246). That points at a per-currency limit applied **without FX conversion** — a pattern that is invisible in any one ticket and only emerges when the USD, EUR and JPY reports are laid side by side.

## Ruled out

- **d5** (web-storefront seasonal theme / CSS refresh) — shipped ~2 days earlier with no tickets in between, and cannot produce server-side 500s (t228) or 30-second server timeouts (t238).
- **Client-side / browser-specific** — reproduces on Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari incl. iOS (t230, t233, t246).
- **Genuine card declines** — banks see no charge attempt (t226).
- **Pre-existing / recurrence** — archive holds only t101, t107, t108, all benign and unrelated (search_ticket_history#2).
- **Out of cluster:** analytics/reporting timeouts t236, t240, t247 — no payment path, no threshold behaviour. Triage separately; **not investigated**.

## Hypotheses (unconfirmed correlations)

1. **d6's enhanced fraud screening rejects or hangs above its high-value threshold**, killing `/v2/transactions` before authorization (d6, t223, t224, t226, t228). *Not examined:* no code, logs or screening config; t228 trace unopened; no rollback test run.
2. **Threshold applied per-currency without FX normalization** — one numeric limit near 1,000 applied to USD, EUR and JPY alike (t224, t233, t238, t243, t246). *Not examined:* no threshold config, FX logic or limit table inspected; inference is from ticket text only.
3. **Mixed surfaces are one upstream fault at different layers** — a hanging screening call surfacing as 500 (t228), 30s timeout (t238), or endless spinner / white screen (t246, t235). *Not examined:* no gateway/service timeout or retry settings, no traces; one-fault-vs-many unconfirmed.

## Suggested repro

1. On payment-service at or after **d6**, `POST /v2/transactions` with a cart just above 1,000 units of local currency (**$1,300**, then **€1,250**, then **¥150,000**). Expect an error page, HTTP 500, or a ~30s hang then timeout — with **no** authorization attempt reaching the card network.
2. Repeat the identical flow with a small cart (**~€40**, or a 5-seat license). Expect success.
3. Bisect the amount in USD, then independently in EUR and JPY, to locate the exact cutoff per currency; per the tickets, expect a bare limit near 1,000 applied without FX conversion.
4. **Mitigation test:** disable enhanced fraud screening / revert d6 and re-run the above-threshold case. If failures stop, causation is established.
5. Pull the **t228 trace** to pin where in the request path the failure occurs.

## Not examined

No code, logs, or fraud-screening configuration were read. The **t228 trace** — the highest-value available evidence — was not opened. Deploys **after 2026-08-11T15:00:00Z** were not queried, so it is unknown whether a later change worsened, mitigated, or rolled back d6; deploys were also not filtered by service, so other services may have changed. Accounts **a02–a09, a11, a12** were never looked up (tier, region, ACV), leaving region spread and revenue exposure incomplete. No revenue or transaction telemetry was queried — the ~$18k figure is customer self-reported (t248). Tickets t236, t240, t247 were not investigated. Whether the 500s, 30-second timeouts and infinite spinners are one fault or several is unconfirmed.

## Recommended next steps

1. Inspect **d6** threshold logic and per-currency handling first; run the revert/disable mitigation test.
2. Pull the **t228** trace.
3. Confirm whether the mixed failure modes are one fault or two.
4. Proactively notify **a01** and **a10** given ACV and active escalation (t248, t230).
